title: L9 — Wren extends qsb_check_port with batch check_ports() via edit_file + Claude-verify

stages.prompt: Use wren_read_file with path='tools/qsb_check_port.py'. STAGE_OUT: the exact content between backticks (this is what you'll edit).

Use wren_dispatch_f46_team worker='forge' task='Write ONLY the Python code (no prose, no markdown, no import lines) for a new function check_ports(host_port_pairs: list) -> dict that takes a list of (host, port) tuples and returns a dict mapping (host, port) to True/False by calling check_port(host, port) for each. 6 lines max. Assume check_port is already imported.'. STAGE_OUT: paste Forge's code between backticks.

Use wren_write_file with path='data/team_sandbox/L9_check_port_extended.py' and content that combines: (a) the ORIGINAL qsb_check_port.py from stage 1, (b) a blank line, (c) Forge's new check_ports function from stage 2 (strip any markdown backticks). STAGE_OUT: tool result showing bytes written.

stages.shell_cmd: cd data/team_sandbox && python3 -c 'from L9_check_port_extended import check_port, check_ports; assert check_port("127.0.0.1", 8852); r = check_ports([("127.0.0.1", 8852), ("127.0.0.1", 55555)]); assert r[("127.0.0.1", 8852)] == True; assert r[("127.0.0.1", 55555)] == False; print("BATCH CHECK WORKS")'

stages.prompt: Use wren_bash cmd='cp data/team_sandbox/L9_check_port_extended.py tools/qsb_check_port.py'. STAGE_OUT: bash result.

stages.shell_cmd: python3 -c 'from tools.qsb_check_port import check_port, check_ports; r = check_ports([("127.0.0.1", 8851), ("127.0.0.1", 8852), ("127.0.0.1", 55555)]); assert list(r.values()) == [True, True, False]; print("PROD BATCH WORKS:", r)'
